title: GB women top group as they aim to book Olympic spot
description: The Great Britain women's team progress as group winners as they aim to secure an Olympic spot at the flag football World Championships.
fullText:
The Great Britain women's team have progressed as group winners at the flag football World Championships as they aim to secure an Olympic spot.

The event in Germany is the first where teams can qualify for Los Angeles 2028, when the non-contact version of American football will make its Olympics debut.

GB women, who are ranked third in the world and are the two-time defending European champions, beat France (33-14) and China (26-25) in their opening two group games on Thursday.

GB then claimed a 47-26 win over Austria on Friday to ensure they went through to the knockout stage as group winners.

If they beat Panama in the quarter-finals on Saturday (09:30 BST) they could face defending champions the USA in the semis later that day.

The top two teams - apart from Olympic hosts America - will qualify for LA28 this weekend, so GB would still get another chance to book their spot in the bronze-medal game.

The GB men's team, ranked 12th in the world, finished bottom of the group after losing to Italy (21-12), France (43-32) and Panama (33-27).

They will now play in ranking matches to decide ninth to 16th place, beginning with a game against Switzerland.

The gold and bronze-medal games will be played on Sunday in Dusseldorf.

title: Ramsay-Peaty confused by early exit at Europeans
description: Former Olympic and world champion Adam Ramsay-Peaty says he is "confused" as his poor run of form continues at the European Aquatics Championships.
fullText:
Former Olympic and world champion Adam Ramsay-Peaty says he is "confused" as the Briton's poor run of form continued at the European Aquatics Championships.

After winning 16 out of 16 golds in the competition between 2014 and 2020, his unbeaten European run ended in Paris this week as he finished fifth in the 100m breaststroke and fourth in the mixed medley relay.

Now the 31-year-old has been unable to reach the 50m breaststroke semi-finals on Friday as he came eighth in his heat.

Ramsay-Peaty set the world record of 25.95 seconds in 2017 but made a poor start to Friday's heat and came home in 27.34secs.

That meant he finished 20th overall, with the 16 fastest qualifying for the semi-finals later on Friday.

"These performances are not good enough at all," he told Swimmingworldmagazine.com. "Even now I am like, it is so bad that I'm confused.

"It's very frustrating, but I'm hoping we can figure it out."

Ramsay-Peaty broke down in tears after winning 100m breaststroke bronze at last month's Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

After settling for another bronze in the 50m he said "nothing makes sense", and although his time improved to 59.10secs in Paris, it was only good enough for fifth.

Ramsay-Peaty has been working on his dive with coach Lisa Bates since June and said the past few weeks have been "one of those lessons".

"It is probably how I'm hitting the water," he added. "I think I've just got to really change up what I'm doing, to be honest."

Compatriot Filip Nowacki, who won 200m gold and 100m silver in Glasgow, finished 18th in the Paris heats so also missed out on the semi-finals.

fullText:
Creative Assembly could strike gold again with this follow-up to their fan-favourite, film-inspired game … if you’re brave enough to venture outdoors

Alien: Isolation redefined Alien games on its release in 2014, bringing the original taut, haunted house theme of the first movie to fans who had mostly been fed action-packed shooters. Cowering under desks and inside lockers wasn’t a new thing; being hunted by an intelligent and lethal xenomorph that could spring down from a duct at any moment was.

“I was thinking about what we could do for a sequel while we were still finishing the first game,” reveals Creative Assembly’s Alistair Hope, creative lead on Alien: Isolation and its sequel. “But we didn’t actually start the project until around the time of the 10th anniversary. We’ve seen the response grow over time, watching [Alien: Isolation] continue to find new players, even though it’s a relatively old game. And they’re surprised there isn’t a sequel.”

Details are slight, but here’s what we know so far: a Weyland-Yutani survey team discovers a crashed vessel on a planet that resembles LV-426 crossed with a windswept forest. It’s a vessel that’ll appear familiar to fans of Alien: Isolation – it’s the part of Sevastopol that the duplicitous Marshal Waits jettisons from the station in the first game, with Amanda Ripley and the alien inside. Ripley escapes. The alien does not. Until now.

“We were super proud of Amanda. She’s really important to the Alien: Isolation experience. But we wanted to tell a new story, in a new location, and to do that, it felt like we needed a new protagonist,” says Hope. That new character is Blake, although Hope is tight-lipped on any details beyond her employer, Weyland-Yutani. It seems likely, however, that this new lead, thrust into the dangerous world of the xenomorph, will follow the IP’s tradition of strong female characters.

A fascinating part of Alien: Isolation 2 will be how the alien reacts to its new environment. “The alien uses its senses to track you down, and it’s very effective in those interior spaces. So we’ve been effectively training it to hunt in the exterior. Those core survival skills that you needed in the first game will be the same – but the player and the alien are going to have to adapt to survive.” That’s not to say Alien: Isolation 2 won’t have plenty of claustrophobic interiors, creating a seesaw of emotions whether trapped inside or exposed outside. “We can play with that, and mess with it. It feels like a really exciting opportunity.”

Taking place months after the events of Alien: Isolation, the sequel will retain the low-fi sci-fi universe, leaning heavily once more on the first Alien movie. There’s a glimpse of a Working Joe in the trailer, suggesting that, once again, the alien might not be the only antagonist the player has to avoid. Could hostile humans enter the mix? Hope is guarded. “Alien: Isolation 2 absolutely is building on that core foundation that we established in the first [game],” he says. “And, yeah, we love that rock, paper, scissors setup and scenario.” Draw your own acid blood-spattered conclusions.

Sevastopol, the decommissioned and slowly decaying space station of Alien: Isolation, became an evocative extra character in the original game. Creative Assembly appears well placed to repeat the trick with Alien: Isolation 2’s forbidding colony world, home to a remote Weyland-Yutani outpost, Kurosaki Station. Just don’t forget your umbrella.

title: I Tried the Android App That's Helping People Around the World Bypass Censorship Laws
description: You can now run Snowflake Volunteer on any Android phone.
fullText:
If you've read our previous coverage on the Tor network and the Tor Browser, you'll know they're the best choices if you want to maximize your privacy and anonymity on the internet. Now, the Tor project has teamed up with the Bloco Android app studio to release another app focused on privacy and anonymity: Snowflake Volunteer.

This isn't only bout keeping your own browsing safe and secure—if you install it on your Android phone, you're helping other people circumvent censorship restrictions in their current location, donating part of your connection to the web so that they can get online at all.

The Tor Browser is so effective at hiding the identity and online activities of users that certain governments would rather their citizens didn't make use of it. That takes away one of the best privacy browsers in the business for the people of those countries, and anyone who happens to be visiting them. Censoring the Tor Browser is usually done by refusing access to the relay nodes that it routes traffic around—the stops on the way to and from the internet that do the job of concealing locations and other identifiable information. However, the relay directory is public, which means it can be blocked.

That's where Snowflake comes in. The standalone Android app is new, but the idea isn't. Snowflake is an alternative way the Tor Browser can get online: A Snowflake connection is disguised as a standard video call over the WebRTC protocol, which isn't typically restricted, and from there, a connection can be made to the Tor network.

With Snowflake on your phone, you're essentially smuggling someone in a Tor-restricted country across the border, digitally speaking. Even if these intermediate bridges are detected and blocked, they're short-lived, with new ones continually popping up, making it virtually impossible for a government to block this method of access without crippling much of the general internet in their country.

The Tor Browser runs as normal for the user who's connecting, albeit with the standard trade-offs in terms of speed and latency. Because of the rerouting and technical borrowing that goes on, Tor isn't the best option if you want to maximize your broadband upload and download speeds.

As a firm believer that internet users should be able to get on the web with a high level of anonymity and privacy, I installed the new Snowflake Volunteer app from the Google Play Store (it's also on F-Droid) and powered it up. The first job is to exempt it from battery management rules so it will stay available even if it's not being used, a process the app guides you through.

That done, all that's required is enabling the toggle switch on the main screen, and your phone is ready and waiting for someone else to connect. There's no setup configuration to work through, no user account to create, and everything works automatically in the background—it really is designed to be as simple as possible.

Tap on the settings cog (top right), and you'll find a few settings at your disposal: You can opt to only allow connections when you're on unmetered networks (such as wifi) or when your phone is charging. You can also set how many users your phone can support at any one time. This is all in the interest of limiting the impact on your device.

Across four hours or so, I saw six connections made, sending a total of 3.2 megabytes and receiving a total of 17 megabytes—hardly excessive use. My phone wasn't suddenly overrun with other users wanting to get online. Snowflake Volunteer is designed as an emergency measure for circumventing censorship, and the usage I've seen backs that up.

I didn't notice any bugs or any problems with the app or any impact on my battery life (perhaps to be expected with so little activity). I think it's something I'll keep switched on, especially overnight when I'm not using my device. It's a nice idea to be able to see the stats on how many people you've helped over time, as an encouragement to keep your device available.

As a Snowflake Volunteer, you're not at risk of being identified by any state that's censored the Tor project: To them, you look like a standard audio or video call connection, and there's no static list of IP addresses to block. What's more, the same multiple layers of encryption that protect the entire Tor network are still in place, so you're unable to see anything connecting users are doing, and they will go through several more nodes before doing any browsing anyway—your device is just the entry point. No one who connects to your device can learn anything about you: The app is simply not capable of any sort of surveillance. You're loaning a slice of connectivity, anonymously and securely. (There are more details of how it all works in Tor's Snowflake documentation.)

The new Android app isn't your only option for putting your hand up as a Snowflake volunteer. You can also install the desktop browser add-on or enable the Kindness Mode in the Orbot app for iOS (a VPN that enables connections to the Tor network).

title: Nigeria to miss Women's World Cup after South Africa and Ghana win play-offs
description: South Africa and Ghana progress to an inter-confederation qualifier for the 2027 Women's World Cup, but Nigeria will miss the tournament for the first time.
fullText:
Nigeria have failed to qualify for the Fifa Women's World Cup for the first time after they were beaten 2-1 by South Africa in a play-off at the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon).

The continent's top-ranked team went into the tournament in Morocco as favourites to retain their title but were eliminated in the quarter-finals by Cameroon, having already lost to Malawi in the group stage.

With the four semi-finalists guaranteed a spot at next year's World Cup, Justin Madugu's side had one more chance to keep alive their hopes of reaching Brazil, with the winner of their one-off tie in Casablanca entering an inter-confederation qualifier.

But second-half goals from Thembi Kgatlana and Refiloe Jane were enough to give Banyana Banyana victory, despite unexpected late drama when Jane was sent off after picking up a second yellow card for handling the ball inside her own six-yard box.

Christy Ucheibe slotted home the penalty in the 93rd minute to set up a grandstand finish, and there was even time for goalkeeper Kaylin Swart, South Africa's hero, to save brilliantly with her feet to deny Michelle Alozie with almost the last kick of the game.

The 2022 Wafcon champions join Ghana in Fifa's inter-confederation qualifier after the Black Queens came from behind to beat Ivory Coast 2-1 earlier on Thursday.

Nigeria have appeared at all nine Women's World Cups since the first was held in China in 1991.

Missing out is unlikely to go down well in a country where football fans are used to their team dominating, with the Super Falcons having won Wafcon a record 10 times.

But seeing off Desiree Ellis' well-drilled Banyana team was never likely to be easy.

While the first half in Casablanca was a non-event, the second period was anything but, with chances aplenty.

Asisat Oshoala should have done better when she bundled her way through several challenges and poked goalwards from inside the six-yard box, failing to get the requisite power on her strike to trouble Swart.

The six-time African footballer of the year was subbed soon after and there will no doubt be questions about whether the 31-year-old might have appeared at her final Wafcon.

The breakthrough came on the counter in the 56th minute, with striker Ronnel Donnelly playing an exquisite through ball from midway inside her own half to set Hildah Magaia free.

Magaia's cross from the left was met by the onrushing Kgatlana, whose shot had enough power to sneak over the line despite keeper Chiamaka Nnadozie getting a strong hand to it.

Nnadozie did keep out another Kgatlana effort five minutes later, while Swart pulled off a stunning save from Uchenna Kanu's header, diving acrobatically to her left to palm the ball away one-handed.

Jane's goal came courtesy of a deflection off Ucheibe's outstretched foot in the 77th minute and Magaia should also have scored when clean through less than a minute after the restart.

It looked as if Nigeria would be unable to create a way back into the game until Jane's unnecessary handball was spotted by the video assistant referee (VAR).

The captain did not need to stretch out her arm, with Swart well placed to save on the goalline.

With the numerical advantage, Nigeria piled on the pressure and almost found salvation in the 97th minute when Alozie drilled the ball back across goal, only to see Swart's left boot shoot out to stop it flying into the bottom corner.

Swart and South Africa celebrated their victory with glee, but a place at the World Cup is far from certain.

They must first negotiate a six-team league alongside Ghana in November and December, with Asian sides Uzbekistan and Chinese Taipei, Papua New Guinea from Oceania and Ecuador from South America also involved.

The top two sides from that mini-league will advance to a final inter-continental qualifier in February, with three sides from that booking their spot in Brazil.

In the earlier game in Casablanca, Ivory Coast were awarded a penalty after just 44 seconds when Bernadette Kakounan was clipped by Princess Marfo.

After a VAR check, Ines Konan converted to give the Lady Elephants a fourth-minute lead despite Ghana keeper Cynthia Konlan getting a hand to the ball.

The Black Queens thought they had equalised early in the second half when Stella Nyamekye stabbed in, but South African referee Akhona Makalima adjudged that Evelyn Badu had kicked the ball out of the hands of Ivorian keeper Oceane Konan moments before.

Ghana did level in the 59th minute, with Marfo heading in from a corner to make amends for her earlier challenge, and the turnaround was complete when Josephine Bonsu scored from the penalty spot in the 72nd minute after VAR had again intervened.

Grace Asantewaa's fierce strike clearly hit the right arm of Ivory Coast defender Aboa Yapo just inside the area, but it took some deliberation and a trip to the pitch-side monitor before Makalima awarded the foul.

Ghana's victory came a day after the Black Queens squad had issued a statement claiming players and officials were awaiting several payments including Wafcon qualification bonuses, group-stage bonuses and per diem allowances.

Ghana's Ministry of Sports and Recreation challenged aspects of the allegations, with sports minister Kofi Adams insisting that per diem payments had already been settled.

A statement from a Ministry official added that the squad's win bonus from their group stage victory over Cape Verde was being processed, and said that the Black Queens qualifying for Wafcon "does not attract a separate bonus".

title: 'Dad rang and I was like: What's happening?' - England U20s boss on Uefa threat
description: England head coach Lydia Bedford says she has been told to "just continue as usual" before next month's Under-20 Women's World Cup, despite the threat of a Uefa boycott over an ongoing row with Fifa.
fullText:
England's head coach Lydia Bedford says she has been told by the Football Association to "just continue as usual" before next month's Under-20 Women's World Cup, despite Uefa threatening to boycott the tournament.

Bedford said she had not "thought too much about the bigger picture" as she prepares to name her Young Lionesses squad next week.

Football has been engulfed in a major dispute since it emerged that Fifa president Gianni Infantino was planning to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors.

Uefa and its 55 members threatened to boycott Fifa competitions, and that still stands despite the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal having been abandoned earlier this month with the Under-20 Women's World Cup the first tournament that could be impacted.

Speaking to BBC Sport in Portugal after England had won a warm-up game against Portugal, Bedford spoke for the first time about the potential boycott.

"I was actually at the theatre in London when my dad rang me out of the blue and I was like 'what's happening?' From my perspective the message from leadership all along has been 'just continue as usual' so we have," she said.

"It's not something we've really even spoken to the players about because ultimately every opportunity we have to get on the grass and prepare this team we want to be in the best position possible.

"So all focus has been on that."

Women's football shouldn't be penalised by Uefa boycott - Nandy

Six European teams are set to take part in the tournament, which runs from 5-27 September, and BBC Sport understands none of them have told hosts Poland that they are withdrawing.

Poland's attacking midfielder Weronika Arasniewicz also spoke to BBC Sport and outlined her opposition to a proposed boycott.

"Don't do it. Let the football be there. Let's enjoy football," Arasniewicz said.

"I would be disappointed for sure [if the tournament was cancelled] because events like this, it's always special and you don't know how many World Cups you have ahead of you."

While some players oppose the boycott, England international Lucy Bronze recently said that boycotting Fifa competitions would be the right thing "for the good of the game", despite the impact it could have on women's football.

Asked about those comments, Bedford said: "From my perspective my only focus is preparing this team to be ready and if we have the opportunity to go to Poland we will be there and punching when we arrive.

"So I haven't thought too much about the bigger picture but my message has been continue as usual and that is what we are going to continue to do."

Bedford was appointed as England women's Under-23s coach in March, and as part of that role is leading the Young Lionesses for the tournament in Poland.

On Thursday, her side beat Portugal U20s 2-0 in a friendly in Lisbon.

"I'm really proud of the players," she said. "From start to finish today we showed our quality and our depth in this squad.

"I have an incredibly difficult decision to make next week to pick the team that finally goes."

fullText:
Newly-signed winger Haissem Hassan says he grew up watching Celtic play in the Champions League and is determined to make the club a regular presence at the top level of European competition.

The 24-year-old, who impressed this summer at the World Cup for Egypt, has joined Martin O'Neill's side as the Champions League play-off first leg with LASK looms next Wednesday.

Hassan, whose arrival was followed by fellow new recruit Mika Baur, said through a translator: "Everything is about winning at Celtic, we have to win every game.

"Being in Europe and in the Champions League, because I think Celtic is a club that belongs in the Champions League.

"I've seen them growing up on the TV, and I think we need to go in the Champions League every season.

"I'm here to help the team win trophies, I'm going in the Champions League every year and make the club better season after season."

Hassan has played for clubs in Spain and France, where he was born, and switched his international allegiance to Egypt earlier this year.

The winger is confident he will be able to adapt quickly to the rigours of Scottish football.

"Scottish football might be a bit more tough, but I think at the end that will make me a more complete player," he said.

"I've already done it in France and Spain, so I think I can adapt here as well. At the end, that will be the best for me as well.

"I also play in Africa with Egypt, and that's another style as well. There is no problem for that."

title: Jon Rahm may be preparing to leave LIV Golf with potential Ryder Cup decision looming
description: With fines and suspensions reportedly coming on the DP World Tour again, Jon Rahm may be the latest to leave LIV Golf in 2027.
fullText:
Jon Rahm may be preparing an exit from LIV Golf.

There are apparently fears within LIV Golf that Rahm, who is undoubtedly one of the biggest names on the breakaway circuit, will leave after the 2026 campaign, according to The Telegraph's James Corrigan. If that comes to fruition, it would be a massive blow to the venture that is trying to find a way to survive beyond the season.

The DP World Tour is "increasingly confident" that Rahm will return next season, too. According to Corrigan, some believe that the European tour has already been primed about his decision.

It's unclear when Rahm will come to a final decision. LIV Golf is set to hold a tournament in Indianapolis next week. It is widely expected to cancel the team championship in Michigan later this month, too, so next week's tournament will be the final one in the 2026 campaign.

The logistics of Rahm's potential split aren't known, either. He still has multiple years left on the reported $300 million deal he first signed to jump over to LIV Golf in the first place. He even said in May that he didn't "see many ways out" of the contract. But, according to Corrigan, Rahm is still owed a "nine-figure" portion of that deal.

Rahm has won 11 times on the PGA Tour in his career. He picked up his only major championship win at the Masters in 2023, though the former top-ranked golfer in the world finished in second at the PGA Championship earlier this year. He's won multiple times with LIV Golf this season, too.

Things aren't solidified just yet, but the breakup between Rahm and LIV would make sense for a number of reasons.

First, LIV Golf's future has been incredibly murky after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund announced earlier this year it would no longer fund the league after the season. That sent the league into turmoil, and left CEO Scott O'Neil and others scrambling to find new financial backers.

LIV announced earlier this month that it had secured an unnamed "lead investor" to find the league for years to come, but specifics were not announced. The name of the investor was kept quiet, too. LIV also announced that golfers would be able to own equity in the league. But Rahm, according to Corrigan, "is not enamored by the prospect of the new LIV iteration."

Then on Wednesday, the DP World Tour reportedly started notifying LIV Golf members that it would resume imposing heavy fines and suspensions as part of its conflicting events rule in 2027. That essentially was the European league drawing a line in the sand and forcing LIV Golf members to choose between them and LIV Golf after it had allowed conditional releases for members to play in this season. Rahm had struck a deal to pay off his fines and resume playing with the DP World Tour this season after a long feud.

Had Rahm not reached that deal, he would have lost his DP World Tour membership and been ineligible for the Ryder Cup in 2027. That league controls the European team, and members must be in good standing with the Tour in order to participate in next year's competition in Ireland. If Rahm ends up staying with LIV Golf next season, his status for the European Ryder Cup team next fall will absolutely be in doubt.

It's unclear where the PGA Tour stands with Rahm. It could force Rahm to serve a one-year suspension, like Patrick Reed had to, in order to return. Or it could offer him a path back like it did with Brooks Koepka earlier this year, which came with heavy fines and restrictions.

But regardless of the specifics or the reasoning, LIV Golf losing Rahm would be just the latest blow for the league this season. Rahm is arguably the biggest name left with LIV Golf, behind only Bryson DeChambeau. Losing him would not only take more eyes away, but would make a pitch to potential new financial backers that much harder to sell.

title: Fighter jets intercept plane over Ohio, where Trump attended event
description: Last month, fighter jets also intercepted planes attempting to fly near MetLife Stadium, during the World Cup Final.
fullText:
(NewsNation) — Fighter jets intercepted a plane that entered restricted airspace Tuesday over Geneva, Ohio, where President Donald Trump was attending an event, military officials said.

F-16 fighter jets used flares to alert the pilot after the plane violated a temporary flight restriction, according to the North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD).

The interception occurred Tuesday around 6:15 p.m. ET. The civilian aircraft was safely escorted out of the restricted airspace.

NORAD said the flares are designed with safety in mind, "burn out quickly and completely, and pose no danger to people on the ground." Officials noted they may have been visible from the ground.

The temporary flight restriction was issued by the Federal Aviation Administration as Trump traveled to Ohio to attend the 2026 Patriot Games, a youth athletic tournament backed by the White House.

The incident comes days after NORAD fighter jets intercepted planes over Bedminster, New Jersey, where Trump owns a golf course. Two general aviation aircraft violated temporary flight restrictions Sunday and were safely escorted out of the restricted airspace.

Officials said the restrictions are intended to protect airspace around sensitive locations and major events.

Last month, fighter jets intercepted multiple planes attempting to fly in temporarily restricted airspace over Bedminster and East Rutherford, N.J. NORAD said flares were deployed to get the attention of two pilots.

The interceptions occurred while international leaders and celebrities gathered in East Rutherford for the World Cup Final at MetLife Stadium.

The FAA issues temporary flight restrictions for a variety of reasons, including major events involving high-profile political figures. Pilots are notified of the restrictions through Notices to Airmen, or NOTAMs, and NORAD and the FAA urged pilots to check those notices before flying.

title: Berrington & Robertson star as Scotland crush Canada
description: Captain Richie Berrington and debutant Lyle Robertson star as Scotland enjoy a thumping 170-run World Cup League 2 victory over Canada at Forthill.
fullText:
ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 tri-series, Forthill

Scotland 347-7 (50 overs): Berrington 120, McMullen 64, Cross 51, Jones 41; Shirzad 4-60

Canada 177 (35 overs): P. Singh 42; Robertson 6-52

Captain Richie Berrington and debutant Lyle Robertson starred as Scotland enjoyed a thumping 170-run Cricket World Cup League 2 victory over Canada at Forthill.

Berrington, 39, hit an impressive 120 as the hosts posted an imposing total of 347 from their 50 overs before Falkland off-spinner Robertson ripped through Canada's batting order, taking six wickets for 52 runs.

Berrington's seventh one-day international century included four sixes, taking his overall haul to 90 - a new Scottish record, overtaking George Munsey's 87.

Brandon McMullen (64) shared a third-wicket partnership of 140 with his captain after the departure of openers Finlay McCreath and Michael English had Scotland on 25-2 in the seventh over.

Michael Jones and Matthew Cross kept up the brisk run rate with knocks of 41 and 51 not out respectively and Jack Jarvis added 30 from 14 balls for a 347-7 total.

Berrington was also involved as Canada lost their first wicket in the third over of their reply, taking a catch from the bowling of Mark Watt.

Pargat Singh (42) was the only Canadian batter to offer any meaningful resistance as Robertson staked his claim for a regular place in the Scotland side.

The 23-year-old picked up his first international wicket as Harsh Thaker picked out Oliver Davidson on the midwicket boundary and his day got even better as he took five scalps from his final 15 deliveries to finish with remarkable figures.

After dismissing Shreyas Movva and Zahid Shirzad in successive balls for his five-wicket haul, Robertson had number 11 Kaleem Sana in his sights for a hat-trick.

That particular feat was not to be, but Robertson ripped one back through bat and pad with the last ball of his spell to seal a massive win and cap a dream debut.

Scotland were already assured of place in the World Cup qualifier after last week's win over the same opponents.

Having beaten the United Arab Emirates on Sunday, the defending champions are now top of the World Cup League 2 standings, although they have played four more matches than the United States, who sit two points behind.

title: Why half of England's World Cup defenders are on the move
description: England came third in this summer's World Cup - their best performance in a men's competition in 60 years - and now their players are in demand in the transfer market.
fullText:
England came third in this summer's World Cup - their best performance in a men's competition in 60 years - and now their players are in demand in the transfer market.

Of the 27 players that went out to North America - 26 in the original squad and Trevoh Chalobah, who replaced the injured Tino Livramento - seven have moved clubs this summer, with another two linked with transfers.

Morgan Rogers went from Aston Villa to Chelsea in a £117m deal, midfielder Elliot Anderson moved for £116m from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City and winger Anthony Gordon cost Barcelona almost £70m when transferring from Newcastle.

Midfielder Jordan Henderson made the short trip across west London on a free transfer to Chelsea after his Brentford contract was mutually terminated and back-up goalkeeper James Trafford signed for Leeds in a £45m move from Manchester City.

But what might be more surprising is how in-demand England's defenders have become - and the low prices they are moving for.

With Djed Spence on the verge of going to Inter Milan, where he could join Three Lions team-mate John Stones, Trevoh Chalobah having moved to Como and Ezri Konsa being targeted by Arsenal, four of England's World Cup defenders will be potentially moving clubs this summer.

But if you go back a bit further, Marc Guehi left Crystal Palace for Manchester City in January and Jarell Quansah moved from Liverpool to Bayer Leverkusen in July 2025 - meaning six of the nine England defenders on World Cup duty could have switched teams in just over a year.

We look at the defenders on the move this summer and explain why they are moving; the push and pull factors involved and what the moves will offer both the player and the clubs involved.

Although attacking players such as Rogers and Gordon and central midfielder Anderson have been involved in massive deals this summer, there has certainly been more value to be found in the defenders.

Tottenham full-back Spence, 26, might only cost Inter Milan £25.6m, despite ending the World Cup strongly, repeatedly displaying his pace and willingness to go forward.

He impressed in the semi-final, including a superb last-ditch sliding challenge to stop Argentina's Giuliano Simeone from scoring.

Spurs finished 17th last season, only clinching Premier League survival on the final day, while Inter Milan are the reigning Serie A champions and also Coppa Italia holders.

Stones, 32, was always going to be in demand as he was available on a free transfer after a hugely-successful spell at Manchester City, winning the Premier League six times and the Champions League once.

The only question was over his fitness, but he answered those worries by featuring in five of England's eight World Cup matches, having played in all five in 2022 and all seven in 2018, when the Three Lions again lost in the semi-finals.

He has played 94 times for England and was also an ever-present in their runs to the European Championship finals in 2021 and 2024 and seems to be a risk-free bargain for Inter.

Konsa, 28, played in all eight World Cup matches this summer, with Arsenal failing with a bid of £30m and Villa holding out for near double that.

But even a transfer of under £50m would prove good value for a player that has played 28 times for his country and helped Villa win the Europa League in May.

Arsenal won the Premier League in 2025-26 and reached the final of the Champions League, but with France centre-half William Saliba set to miss an "extended period" because of a back injury, they are in need for an instant high-level replacement, which Konsa would be.

Chalobah, 27, only featured in the third-fourth play-off, which England won 6-4 against France in a crazy game in Miami as he earned his second international cap.

However, his transfer to Italian side Como, who are managed by ex-Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas and qualified for the Champions League for the first time in their history, still comes in at the cheaper end of the market.

Chelsea will receive an initial £25.7m, with a further £5.1m possible in add-ons, while France defender Maxence Lacroix, signed from Crystal Palace, cost the Blues much more at £52m.

Chalobah had been at Chelsea since the age of eight, winning the FA Cup, Conference League and Fifa Club World Cup twice - playing all 90 minutes of the final as the Blues beat Paris St-Germain 3-0 in 2025.

But with the arrival of Lacroix and with numerous other central defensive options, including Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Axel Disasi, Tosin Adarabioyo, Benoit Badiashile and Jorrel Hato, Chalobah has opted for more guaranteed first-team football.

Guehi, 26, another who played in all of England's World Cup games, only cost Manchester City £20m in January as his Crystal Palace contract was expiring in six months.

It was a similar story for right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold, surprisingly left out of Thomas Tuchel's World Cup squad after a season at Real Madrid, who only paid Liverpool £8.5m in May 2025 with his Anfield deal coming to an end.

The most expensive move among the names mentioned was Quansah's £35m move from Liverpool to Bayer Leverkusen last summer, although the fact he was only 22 at the time was one of the reasons for the German side paying more.

In the past eight years, England have reached two World Cup semi-finals, one quarter-final and the final of two European Championships.

Firstly under Gareth Southgate and then under Thomas Tuchel, the Three Lions have generally been well organised, hard to break down and tough to beat - with defensive players being able to shine.

When they finished fourth in the 2018 World Cup, they conceded only eight goals in seven games and it was the same figures in 2026 in their opening seven matches, before the madness of the 6-4 win over France.

They only conceded twice in seven games in the European Championship in 2021 and six in seven matches at Euro 2024, losing in the final on both occasions.

Under Tuchel, England did not concede a single goal in qualifying for the 2026 World Cup, winning all eight qualifiers and keeping clean sheets in all of them to get to North America with a maximum 24 points.

An attacking and exciting 4-2 win over Croatia in their 2026 opener, led to many thinking there had been a change of philosophy, before England then kept two clean sheets in a row in their other group matches.

England's resolute defending was typified in the last-16 3-2 win over co-hosts Mexico, with Tuchel's side hanging on, despite playing the final 40 minutes with 10 men after Quansah had been sent off.

Similar defensive qualities saw off Norway and star striker Erling Haaland in the quarter-finals, but they could not repeat the trick late on in their semi-final when Argentina, inspired by Lionel Messi, scored twice late on to end English hopes of glory.

title: Henriques chasing 'cricket nirvana' with Portugal
description: Moises Henriques says helping Portugal qualify for their first-ever men's T20 World Cup would be cricket "nirvana" at the twilight of his playing career.
fullText:
Moises Henriques says helping Portugal qualify for their first-ever men's T20 World Cup would be cricket "nirvana" at the twilight of his playing career.

Henriques played four Tests, 16 one-day internationals and 24 T20s for Australia between 2009 and 2021.

The 39-year-old has switched allegiances to Portugal, the country of his birth, and will captain the team at a European sub-regional qualifying tournament in Finland starting on Friday.

Italy played at their maiden T20 World Cup earlier this year having started their campaign at the same level as Portugal.

Henriques said he "didn't even know Portugal had a cricket team" until five years ago but has been impressed by the quality of their squad.

"Obviously, the ideal, the nirvana, would be to replicate what Italy have done," Henriques told the BBC Stumped podcast.

"Whether that's realistic for this World Cup, or the following, I don't know. We'll only be able to tell in a couple games.

"I'm sure there's a lot of opposition that feel that they might be able to do something similar."

Henriques was born in Funchal on the island of Madeira but arrived in Australia aged two when his father Alvaro decided to up sticks and move the family to Sydney in search of a better life.

Alvaro, who played second division football in Portugal, took a job working in a warehouse, where he is still employed today.

Moises and his two younger brothers threw themselves into the Australian way of life, and that meant cricket.

"Moises isn't the most common name going around in an Australian school, especially at that time," Henriques explained.

"I had a few issues at school early on. I didn't speak English that well.

"Cricket gave me that little bit of confidence I probably needed as a kid to feel a part of something."

Stumped podcast: Should the ICC make the Cricket World Cup bigger?

Madeira's most famous son is Cristiano Ronaldo, and the island changed the name of its airport in honour of the Portuguese football star.

Henriques joked he "might get a helicopter pad" named after him, if he is able to skipper Portugal to the World Cup.

Portugal, ranked 37th in the world, will first have to come through the 10-team tournament in Finland, where they have drawn Czech Republic, Germany, Greece and Israel in Group B.

Should they progress, the next stage will be a European final regional qualifier with Scotland, Jersey and Denmark next year.

Henriques said while earning a Baggy Green will take some beating, the feeling of pulling on a Portugal shirt, and captaining the country, will be something special.

"I went back to Madeira last year and it was the first time I'd been back, but I felt really connected to the place," Henriques said.

"When I played for Australia, my family also felt I was representing them as well. I'm representing the motherland, so to speak, and it's going to feel somewhat similar.

"Hopefully we can make a positive impact trying to grow the sport in Portugal and probably Europe more broadly as well."

Henriques, who will also play for Glasgow Cosmic in the inaugural European T20 Premier League following the qualifier, is not the only player in Portugal's squad to have played professionally.

Batter Cameron Shekleton, 26, has played first-class cricket in South Africa and appeared for the Proteas A side.

Former New Zealand Under-19 captain Craig Cachopa, 34, represented Sussex, Auckland and Wellington.

"I was quietly and pleasantly surprised with the quality of cricketers that we've got in the team," Henriques said.

"There's a lot of high-level cricketers going around, which I probably wasn't expecting a few years ago when I first started entertaining the thought of playing."

One challenge that Henriques will face at the qualifier in Finland is playing on an artificial pitch for the first time in a few decades.

"It would be 25 years since I've actually played a game of cricket on a synthetic wicket," added the former Sydney Sixers skipper.

"I'm coming out of back surgery about five months ago so the biggest challenge bowling will be landing on a synthetic wicket on coming off a full run-up.

"Obviously we train a lot indoors on synthetic wickets so hopefully I can make the adjustment."

title: Barcelona forward’s move to PSG set to be completed today or tomorrow
description: After Ronald Araujo, Ferran Torres is set to become the next Barcelona player to leave the club.The Spanish international is widely expected to join Paris Saint-Germain after a brilliant 2025/26 and W...
fullText:
After Ronald Araujo, Ferran Torres is set to become the next Barcelona player to leave the club.

The Spanish international is widely expected to join Paris Saint-Germain after a brilliant 2025/26 and World Cup campaign.

Ferran's move is currently of when and not if; with the player soon expected to travel to the French capital.

According to Cadena SER, the agreement between Barcelona and PSG for Ferran's transfer could be finalised between today and tomorrow.

Ferran Torres to soon become a PSG player. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images)

The forward already has an agreement in place with the French club and is ready to travel to Paris in the coming hours to undergo his medical.

Ferran did not train with Barcelona on Thursday, having also been excused the previous day.

Negotiations between the two clubs have entered their final phase, with PSG having long since agreed personal terms with the player.

All that remains is for the definitive transfer terms to be settled, with the operation set to be closed for a figure of around €55 million.

For Barcelona, recouping such a sum for a player with just one year left on his contract represents excellent business, even if losing a World Cup final hero is far from ideal.

Ferran's exit could pave the way for Rodri to join Barcelona. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images)

Ferran's exit is closely tied to Barcelona's other major ongoing operation, the pursuit of Rodri.

The Catalans have already sent Manchester City a second proposal worth €60 million, made up of a fixed fee and variables, having seen an initial €50 million bid rejected.

However, reports suggest City have also turned down this latest offer.

Barcelona remain confident the deal will ultimately happen, with the club planning to make a third and definitive offer in the region of €70 million, comprising €60 million fixed plus €10 million in add-ons.

The funds generated by Ferran's departure will naturally aid Barcelona's efforts to get the Rodri deal over the line, both financially and in terms of squad registration.

With one exit nearing completion, the Catalans will hope it paves the way for a marquee arrival, as they look to reshape their squad before the window closes.

title: Keely Hodgkinson’s main rival advanced to 800m final after shock fall
description: Audrey Werro, the fastest woman in the world this year, fell and finished last – but was advanced to the 10-athlete final following an appeal
fullText:
Keely Hodgkinson's main rival, Audrey Werro, was advanced to the 800m final at the European Athletics Championships after a shock result in her semi-final as she fell hard and finished last.

Werro, the fastest woman in the world this year, led the first semi-final from the start and responded to accelerations from Britain's Jemma Reekie and French record holder Anais Bourgoin.

But the 22-year-old appeared to be clipped from behind on the final bend and hit the deck hard, with Lithuania's Gabija Galvydyte also falling as the other runners attempted to evade the fallen Swiss.

Both athletes eventually got to their feet and finished the race, with Werro crossing the line last looking heavily winded and clutching her ribs. Referees advanced both her and Galvydyte to the final after appeals, meaning 10 athletes will race for the title on Friday.

Hodgkinson eased to victory in her semi-final, winning in 1:57.38 from Femke Broeders-Bol, who looked comfortable on her shoulder in an unfamiliar event for the Dutchwoman, having stepped up from her usual 400m hurdles this year. The result leaves the pair and Werro on course for a blockbuster clash in Friday's final.

Werro told the BBC afterwards: "I was feeling really great until the last metre, unfortunately, I don't know, something happened and I was on the ground. I hope I will be qualified for the final."

She confirmed that she kept running in order to be able to appeal for a place in the final, if video replays suggested she was hindered by another athlete: "This is the reason why I finished the race and it's always important to go until the end, now we will see what happened."

Reekie came through to win the semi-final in 1:58.61, with Bourgoin and Switzerland's Veronica Vancardo completing the trio of automatic qualifiers.

Werro ran the fastest time in four decades earlier this season, with her new personal best of 1:53.80 the third-fastest of all time, making her the favourite to take gold in Birmingham's Alexander Stadium despite the presence of Olympic champion Hodgkinson and Broeders-Bol.

In the second semi-final Hodgkinson hit the front early with Broeders-Bol latching onto her shoulder, with the pair pulling away in the home straight. Italy's Eloisa Coiro, who set a new national record in the first round, was the last of the automatic qualifiers. Switzerland's Valentina Rosamilia and France's Clara Liberman complete the line-up for the final.

Hodgkinson was asked by BBC Sport whether she had seen Werro's fall. She said: "I heard a 'oohhh' [from the crowd] which is never a good sign; I don't know what it looked like," she said. "You can't worry about what other people are doing [in your race]. It's a real shame, I hope she's okay and that she's in the final tomorrow.

"The depth was really good, another 1:57, overall happy, can't complain. The excitement [for the women's 800m] makes me excited, I love a good challenge, it brings out the best in me.

"I hope for a clean race with no falling over. And no wind please, I'm going to talk to an Esty witch to make sure there's no wind," she smiled.

Broeders-Bol meanwhile said seeing Werro fall had made her feel "extra cautious" in her semi. She said her plan had been to lead "from the front, either with Keely or in front of Keely, I think it worked out perfectly.

"I saw it [the fall], I didn't watch a replay because it often looks terrible. I hope she's okay. It made me extra cautious."

title: ‘It’s time to change’ – Fabrizio Romano teases major shift to football transfer reporting after window closes
description: Fabrizio Romano has revolutionised football transfer reporting, building an enormous global following around his ability to break major moves. Romano first broke the news of Mauro Icardi’s move to Inter Milan in 2011 and has since become the world’s most recognisable football reporter.
fullText:
Fabrizio Romano has revolutionised football transfer reporting, building an enormous global following around his ability to break major moves.

Romano first broke the news of Mauro Icardi's move to Inter Milan in 2011 and has since become the world's most recognisable football reporter.

The Italian journalist has amassed more than 100 million social media followers and popularised the now-famous catchphrase, "here we go".

Romano has continued to break several huge stories throughout the summer, but his latest comments suggest a major change to his approach is on the horizon.

Fabrizio Romano celebrated the success of his report on Ronald Araujo's loan move from Barcelona to Liverpool on LinkedIn.

His exclusive story racked up 49 million views, two million likes, 47,000 comments, and was shared two million times.

However, in the same post, Romano hinted that this could be his final summer as a football transfer reporter.

He wrote: "I'm probably not gonna continue into the transfer market industry as I'm doing right now for longer: it's time to change the approach, the view…

"But this will be another topic soon, after the transfer window closes. But still, these numbers feel incredible.

"The adrenaline of the breaking story, the exclusivity, the unexpected factor, from zero links at all to done deal… well, this will always remain unmatched for me. Onto the next one!"

Whatever comes next for Romano, the football landscape would certainly look different without one of its loudest voices.

description: Pre-game, captain John McGinn promised Aston Villa fans they could still expect "as much as possible" this season despite the high-profile exits of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans.  A battling performance in Austria backed those words up as, even in this defeat by PSG, Villa scared the European champions for a second time in 18 months, following their 5-4 Champions League last-eight defeat in 2025. fullText:
Pre-game, captain John McGinn promised Aston Villa fans they could still expect "as much as possible" this season despite the high-profile exits of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans.

A battling performance in Austria backed those words up as, even in this defeat by PSG, Villa scared the European champions for a second time in 18 months, following their 5-4 Champions League last-eight defeat in 2025.

No Ollie Watkins, Emi Martinez and Ezri Konsa - given more time off after the World Cup - which allowed teenager Brian Madjo to finally show what he can do after Villa won their appeal to register him, and 19-year-old midfielder George Hemmings also getting a start.

The positives were also evident despite the loss, with Boubacar Kamara also playing his first competitive match since a serious knee injury in January.

Villa should be stronger for the Premier League season opener at Brighton on 23 August, with the club due to be active in the final two weeks of the transfer window.

Atletico Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri is poised to join this week, while they have not given up on their chase for Bayern Munich midfielder Joao Palhinha.

Ever the perfectionist, boss Emery will be frustrated by the loss - especially as it was his fourth defeat in the competition - but as Villa enter a new era there is a lot of cause for optimism.

title: Hamilton West Side tops Kentucky, reaches Little League World Series
description: The Hamilton West Side Little League baseball team has reached the Little League World Series for the first time since 2021.
fullText:
The Hamilton West Side Little League baseball team has reached the Little League World Series for the first time since 2021 after defeating Kentucky's North Oldham, 6-0, in Whitestown, Indiana, in the Great Lakes region championship game on ESPN2.

The 2026 Little League World Series begins on Wednesday, Aug. 19, in Williamsport, Pennsylvania. As the Great Lakes region winner, West Side will face the yet-to-be-determined Mountain Region champion on Aug. 20 at 2 p.m.

West Side starter Boone Treadway, the son of Badin head coach Brion Treadway, pitched a one-hit, complete-game shutout. He threw 62 pitches, and struck out nine.

"Feels amazing," Treadway told ESPN after the game. "I'm just glad to get to do it with this group of kids."

Josiah Infante hit a two-run homer during West Side's six-run first inning.

West Side is a 23-time Ohio state champion. In 2021, West Side advanced to the LLWS final before losing to Michigan.

West Side and North Oldham met twice in the Great Lakes regional. West Side won the first meeting, 11-4.

West Side cruised past Michigan and Indiana in the first two rounds of the tournament.

title: Sara Curtis of Italy breaks world record in 50m backstroke
description: Sara Curtis took two tenths off Australian Kaylee McKeown's world record.
fullText:
Italian Sara Curtis broke the world record in the 50m backstroke at the European Swimming Championships in Paris.

Curtis, a University of Virginia rising sophomore, clocked 26.63 seconds in Wednesday's semifinals, taking 23 hundredths off Australian Kaylee McKeown's world record of 26.86 set in 2023.

The 50m backstroke makes its Olympic debut in 2028, along with the 50m breaststroke and 50m butterfly. The 50m freestyle has been on the Olympic program since 1988.

Curtis made her Olympic debut in 2024, reaching the semifinals of the 50m free and placing eighth with the Italian women's 4x100m free relay.

Curtis' previous personal best was 27.07 seconds, ranking her fifth on the all-time performer list before today's world record.

Also at Europeans, Olympic champion Hubert Kos of Hungary swam the second-fastest men's 200m backstroke in history in Tuesday's semifinals — a 1:52.30, second only to American Aaron Peirsol's world record of 1:51.92 from 2009. The men's 200m back is one of just three individual world records still standing from the super-suit era of 2008-09.

Romanian David Popovici swam the third-fastest men's 100m free in history — a 46.56, just off China's Pan Zhanle's world record of 46.40 from the 2024 Olympics. Popovici also has the second-fastest time in history, a 46.51 from winning the 2025 World title.

Swede Sarah Sjostrom won the women's 50m butterfly at Europeans, her 97th career medal among the Olympics, World Championships (long course and short course) and Europeans (long course and short course) and her first since becoming a mom last August.

title: Lampard believes Haji Wright ready for Premier League
description: After struggling to find the field during the World Cup, Wright is ready to lead Coventry into the Premiership.
fullText:
The 2026-27 Premier League season begins next week, and 20 teams enter with dreams renewed for the new year. For Coventry City, who earned promotion to the Premier League after winning the EFL Championship, it will be a chance to compete in the top flight for the first time since the 2000-01 season. And USMNT forward Haji Wright will be a big part of their offense this season.

Wright was one of the major factors behind Coventry's promotion last season, with 18 goals and 2 assists in 40 appearances for the Sky Blues across all competitions. However, he struggled to find any playing time for the USMNT during the 2026 World Cup, with just two minute-long appearances logged for the tournament.

Still, Coventry has relied on him to score goals, and he's done that since he arrived there in August 2023. In 124 total appearances, he's scored 49 goals and added 11 assists. It's that kind of production that head coach Frank Lampard feels has prepared Haji Wright for the rigors of the Premier League.

"When you come into a job, you evaluate the talent in the squad and the need for goals at the top end of the pitch. Haji already had a record as such," Lampard said, speaking exclusively to Stars & Stripes FC. "He was playing on the left wing sometimes under the previous manager, but I felt quite quickly that he's a No. 9 and he prefers to be in that position too. I think it makes the most of his talents and attributes, with his speed, size and ability to run in behind defenses. It will be a big test for him, as with all the players, because there's a big gap with the Premier League. They must be focused on bridging that gap with belief. I think Haji absolutely has the talent to succeed here in the Premier League."

For Lampard, the hope is that Wright is able to continue his goal production to help keep Coventry in the top flight. Most teams that are promoted to the Premier League struggle in that first season, with a big percentage of them getting relegated back to the Championship after one year. Coventry hope to dodge the relegation slide and do what they can to stay afloat. And for Wright, it's a chance to show that he is a dependable striker in one of the best leagues in the world and that he can produce against some of the best defenses on the planet.

Coventry have a tall task ahead of them, as they open up the season on the road on August 21st to defending Premier League champions Arsenal. Three of their first four matches will come against teams that finished in the top 8 in last season's table: Arsenal, Manchester City, and Brighton & Hove Albion. It will truly be a big test for Haji Wright and the Sky Blues as they prepare for their first Premier League season in 25 years.

title: History Says Red Sox Have 50% Chance to Win World Series for This Reason

fullText:
History Says Red Sox Have 50% Chance to Win World Series for This Reason originally appeared on NESN. 

Going 27-3 at any stretch in a season in Major League Baseball is flat-out ridiculous. There's a reason why what the Boston Red Sox did was historic, though it doesn't necessarily guarantee that they're going to win a World Series.

Boston was 37-48 before their streak and was 14 games under .500 at one point. Every other team was above .500 by multiple games before their stretch. What makes matters even more interesting is that three of the six won a World Series.

"1936 Giants 49-44 Lost World Series 1941 Yankees 33-24 Won World Series 1947 Yankees 27-23 Won World Series 1953 Yankees 17-9 Won World Series 1977 Royals 64-51 Lost ALCS 2017 Indians 69-56 Lost ALDS," ESPN posted.

A 50% chance for the Red Sox here, history-wise, is pretty much as good a chance as any other team in Major League Baseball has ever had.

Obviously, there's no guarantee that Boston will even come close to winning the World Series, as this season has been very strange. However, history says that a 50% chance is in the works.

title: Dubois unification moves closer as Turhan joins MVP
description: Turkish lightweight world champion Elif Nur Turhan signs with Most Valuable Promotions, bringing a potential unification fight with Briton Caroline Dubois a step closer.
fullText:
Turkish lightweight world champion Elif Nur Turhan has signed with Most Valuable Promotions, bringing a potential unification fight with Briton Caroline Dubois a step closer.

Turhan was previously signed to Matchroom Boxing but joins MVP as part of a new strategic alliance between the two promotions.

The 31-year-old has won all 14 of her professional bouts, with eight victories by stoppage, and holds the IBF lightweight title.

"Forces have been joined. As female boxers, we will now move forward with greater strength," Turhan said.

"I am excited for the opportunities that will come my way as I look to win more major world titles."

Londoner Dubois - also with MVP - will defend her WBC and WBO lightweight titles against American Amelia Moore on 29 August on an all-female card in Birmingham.

American Stephanie Han, the WBA lightweight champion, is also signed to MVP.

"The Golden Turkish Warrior [Turhan] is one of the most exciting fighters in boxing given her immense punching power and her relentless aggressive, pressure heavy style," MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian said.

"Signing Elif will allow us to make some of the most exciting fights in boxing."

Last month, MVP announced the new partnership with Matchroom, designed to create more opportunities for female fighters across both promotional rosters.

The agreement is expected to create more crossover opportunities, allowing fighters from both promotions to compete on each other's cards.

Turhan joins Australian two-weight world champion Skye Nicolson in making the move from Matchroom to MVP.

MVP also merged with the Professional Fighters League in July to bring together a roster of more than 300 fighters across boxing and mixed martial arts (MMA).

title: GB dressage team qualify for LA28 Olympics

fullText:
The Great Britain dressage team secured qualification for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles by winning silver at the FEI World Championships in Aachen, Germany.

Fiona Bigwood, Charlotte Fry, Carl Hester and Becky Moody finished on a score of 231.4 in the dressage team final, with home nation Germany taking gold on 235.0.

Bigwood, aboard Donna Bella, and Moody, on Jagerbomb, had put GB into second spot on Tuesday.

Hester, on Fame, and defending individual and freestyle world champion Fry, who rode Glamourdale and top scored for the team with 80.311, went on Wednesday and secured second spot.

title: O'Sullivan suffers another setback with China Open exit
description: Ronnie O'Sullivan suffers another defeat as his poor start to the season continued with a 6-4 loss to Noppon Saengkham in the second round of the China Open, with world champion Wu Yize also out.
fullText:
Ronnie O'Sullivan suffered another setback as his poor start to the season continued with a 6-4 loss to Noppon Saengkham in the second round of the China Open.

The 50-year-old, who has won the tournament twice, was 3-1 up before losing four straight frames.

The seven-time world champion responded before losing the final frame 64-46 to add to his second-round exit at the Shanghai Masters last month.

Thailand's Saengkham is ranked 45th in the world and has now beaten O'Sullivan in back-to-back matches.

title: Neto attracting Premier League interest
description: Chelsea winger Pedro Neto has attracted interest from four Premier League clubs, with one believed to be Manchester City.  The 26-year-old Portugal international is not regarded as one of the 'untouchable' players at Stamford Bridge and could therefore move before the transfer deadline.  The club believe the market for wide forwards has been inflated by a lack of options for leading clubs, highlighted by the £117m fee paid for Morgan Rogers and Paris St-Germain's £145m valuation of Bradley Barcola.
fullText:
Chelsea winger Pedro Neto has attracted interest from four Premier League clubs, with one believed to be Manchester City.

The 26-year-old Portugal international is not regarded as one of the 'untouchable' players at Stamford Bridge and could therefore move before the transfer deadline.

However, Chelsea insist they would demand a significant fee for the attacker, who joined from Wolves for £54m in 2024.

The club believe the market for wide forwards has been inflated by a lack of options for leading clubs, highlighted by the £117m fee paid for Morgan Rogers and Paris St-Germain's £145m valuation of Bradley Barcola.

Those figures have influenced Chelsea's valuation of Neto, who is known to be of interest to Manchester City where he would be reunited with former Blues boss Enzo Maresca.

Maresca and Neto are understood to have a strong relationship, and the winger is among those reported to have been frustrated by the Italian's departure midway through last season.

New manager Xabi Alonso has not commented on Neto's future, but he has played the winger in pre-season friendlies, including the 3-0 win over AC Milan on Saturday.

title: Bayonne now one win away from advancing to Little League World Series
description: Bayonne Little League is closing in on history, one win away from becoming the first Hudson County team to advance to the Little League World Series.
fullText:
Bayonne Little League is closing in on history.

With a win in Friday night's Metro Region championship game, the reigning New Jersey state champions would advance to the Little League World Series, becoming the first Hudson County team to accomplish the feat and first New Jersey charter since Toms River East did it in 2021.

Bayonne will face the winner of Game 5 between New York (PYA Port Washington) and Connecticut (Darien) in the Aug. 14 championship game. The New Jersey state champions have already secured a spot in the title matchup after opening the Metro Region tournament with convincing victories over Connecticut and New York.

Bayonne (13-0) won both its games this week in Bristol, Connecticut, outscoring its first two opponents, 20-4. The Bees have been dominant, opening with an 8-2 victory over Connecticut before overwhelming New York, 12-2, two days later.

More: Bayonne Little League in Metro Region: Scores, schedule, TV info

More: Get to know Bayonne Little League players as region tournament begins

In the win over New York, Mason Rincon set the tone early by blasting a two-run home run to center field. Later in the first inning, AJ Tapia lined a single down the right-field line to drive in two more runs, giving Bayonne a 4-0 lead after one inning.

Bayonne continued to pour on the offense, adding one run in the second inning, five 

Gabriel Garcia Jr. and Mason Rincon combined to pitch all four innings, with Garcia earning the victory. He worked the first two innings, allowing three hits and two earned runs while helping keep the Bees firmly in control. Rincon handled the final two innings as Bayonne closed out the 12-2 win under the run rule.

Since Bayonne has not played since Aug. 10, the team will have had several days to rest and prepare for the championship game.

Check out the photo gallery, then 

The winner of the tournament represents the region at the Little League World Series from Aug. 19-30 at the Little League International Complex, Lamade and Volunteer Stadiums in South Williamsport, Pennsylvania.

In the 78 years since the first Little League World Series tournament, only 20 New Jersey teams have qualified for the August classic. Toms River East (2021) is the last New Jersey team to reach a World Series and first since Elmora Youth (Elizabeth) in 2019.

Only four New Jersey teams – Hammonton (1949), Wayne American (1970), Lakewood (1975) and Tom River East American (1998) – have won Little League World Series titles.

Matchup: New Jersey (Bayonne) vs. Game 5 winner between New York (PY A)/Connecticut (Darien).

Location: A. Bartlett Giamatti Little League Leadership Training Center, 335 Mix Street, Bristol, Connecticut.

Fans back home looking to catch Bayonne play can tune into ESPN for full coverage.

Weather has been a recurring factor in Bristol this week, with some games postponed and rescheduled because of intermittent rain. While additional inclement weather is expected in the area on Thursday, conditions are forecasted to improve significantly by Friday. Skies are expected to be clear and sunny, with temperatures around 65 degrees at game time.

Temperatures in Bristol have generally remained in the upper 70s to low 80s throughout the week.

fullText:
Jose Mourinho finally has his full Real Madrid squad back together after Jude Bellingham returned to training following his extended summer break.

The England international completed his commercial commitments in London before making his way back to the club, becoming the final World Cup international to report for duty.

As the clubBellingham took part in the afternoon session alongside the players who were not selected for Real Madrid's Teresa Herrera Trophy meeting with Deportivo La Coruna at Riazor.

His return will be welcomed by Mourinho, who has been gradually integrating the squad ahead of the new season.

The midfielder is also said to be in excellent physical condition, meaning there should be little concern over his fitness as he begins his preparations.

However, Bellingham will not feature against Deportivo.

Bellingham's arrival completes an important stage of Real Madrid's pre-season preparations.

The 23-year-old had been given additional time away following his international commitments, while several of his teammates had already returned to work earlier in the week.

Mourinho now has the majority of his senior group available, although the players who recently reported back are still being managed carefully.

Bellingham trained with and without the ball during the session, beginning the process of getting back up to full match sharpness.

The midfielder was joined by the injured members of the squad, although those players followed individual programmes.

Jude Bellingham is the last player to rejoin training after the World Cup. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

As such, the likes of Raul Asencio, Rodrygo, Eder Militao, Ferland Mendy and Thiago Pitarch were among those continuing their recovery work away from the main group.

Bellingham's first opportunity to play under Mourinho is now expected to come against Schalke on Sunday, August 16.

That gives him several days to work with the first-team group and become accustomed to Mourinho's methods before stepping onto the pitch.

Speaking of the Teresa Herrera Trophy, Kylian Mbappe, Marc Cucurella, Ibrahima Konate and Aurelien Tchouameni are all unavailable for the trip to Riazor despite having returned to training earlier this week.

Rather than immediately throwing the returning internationals into action, Mourinho is giving them time to build their fitness and adapt to the workload.

title: Torres misses Barcelona training to finalise PSG move
description: Spain's World Cup hero Ferran Torres is given permission to miss Barcelona training to finalise a move to Paris St-Germain.
fullText:
Spain's World Cup hero Ferran Torres has been given permission to miss Barcelona training to finalise a move to Paris St-Germain.

Torres, 26, scored an extra-time winner against Argentina to help Spain claim their second World Cup this summer.

He had been due to return to training with the Catalan giants on Wednesday but will not do so as a move to PSG gets closer.

The deal with PSG, who play in the Super Cup final against Aston Villa on Wednesday night in Salzburg, is likely to be worth more than £40m.

Torres only has one year left on his contract at Barcelona and some fans have been frustrated that the forward has spoken openly about the possibility of leaving the club.

Speaking on a media tour of the United States following Spain's World Cup win, he said: "I have a contract with Barcelona but, in football, you never know."

Asked directly about links with PSG, he added: "Every time these teams want you it's a good thing.

"You never know because in football everything can change in one minute, so I have to be ready for everything."

PSG have won the Champions League in the past two seasons and are managed by former Barcelona coach and player Luis Enrique.

The Parisians could lose Bradley Barcola this summer, with the forward wanted by Liverpool.

Torres has been at Barcelona since 2022 having previously spent two years at Manchester City. He has scored 25 goals in 65 appearances for Spain.

title: England gearing up for WXV with new smaller balls
description: England's Red Roses are in pre-season training before the upcoming WXV Global Series and have been using the controversial smaller balls.
fullText:
England's women are in Nottingham for pre-season this month before the upcoming WXV Global Series.

In the new competition, the Red Roses will take on Australia, Canada and New Zealand on home soil in September before further tests across the Atlantic against Canada again and the USA in October.

The last time we saw the world champions in action they were winning another Six Nations' Grand Slam - so what's new?

Head coach John Mitchell spills the beans.

World Rugby's new size 4.5 balls - about 3% smaller but the same weight as a regulation size five - will be used for the WXV Global Series and are now in use in the England camp.

Their introduction has not been without controversy. In May, England fly-half Zoe Harrison said it is "the worst decision someone has ever made".

Mitchell said the attacking players and kickers were all given one to take home for the holidays but he believes "coaching" was key to the success of teams using it.

"If you want to get better at something, regardless of the size of the ball, it's all about coaching. So I think our girls have been well-coached," he said.

"I think it's too early for for me to say that it's going to help our offloading game or it's going to help out with the pass. I'm sure there's consequences as well.

"There might be more contestable kicking, which is probably something that we want to keep away from our game because it's a point of difference between our game and the men's game."

World Rugby held a trial for the smaller balls with female players on the top-tier Sevens circuit in November.

Mitchell said the trial "certainly might help other teams" but he added conclusions would likely be drawn after the first three Tests at home.

During the summer break, Mitchell officially became a UK citizen, external - something he says he should have done "20 years earlier".

Born and raised in New Zealand, the 62-year-old coached the All Blacks to the semi-finals of the 2003 Rugby World Cup but spent much of his early coaching career in England with Sale Sharks, Wasps and as England men's forwards coach.

The citizenship test involves questions about British history and geography as well as singing the national anthem.

Mitchell said his examiner was struggling to find the national anthem music for him so he happily helped her out, explaining: "'I've got it on my Apple Music, is it OK if I play it?' So I played it and I belted it out, and she goes, 'No-one's ever done that before'.

"I said, 'I've had plenty of practice'."

Last month, Gloucester-Hartpury wing Mia Venner and Exeter scrum-half Flo Robinson were awarded full-time England contracts for the first time, among 32 deals for the 2026-27 season.

When asked about Venner and Robinson's contracts, Mitchell said scrum-half Robinson could be an important part of England's plans.

"Will we get Mo [Natasha Hunt] to the next World Cup? We don't know. So it's very important to make sure that we're growing our next player and Flo's definitely taking that on," he said.

Both Gloucester-Hartpury's Hunt, at age 37, and Harlequins' Marlie Packer, 36, are double world champions and included on the Red Roses' latest contract round.

But with Packer admitting she had considered retirement last season, Mitchell explained that for either player to move on, "somebody's got to come and get their jersey" first.

In the off-season it was confirmed Emily Scarratt had joined the Red Roses set-up full-time as attack and backs coach.

Having taken the role on an interim basis during the Six Nations, Mitchell said that the coaching group is "smarter" with Scarratt's inclusion.

However, the new contract appears to come with more responsibility for the former world player of the year.

Mitchell worked with Scarratt on the attack last season but that will start to evolve. He said: "When Em first started, I didn't want to overwhelm her with a with a whole lot of stuff so I gave her a pretty tight remit.

"You just give away a little bit... She certainly has the ability to take the total attack."

The new WXV Global Series doesn't have a table or a trophy attached to it - it is just Test matches.

"There's no tournament to win so we can be very patient about how we go about things," said Mitchell.

Among the six England games are three against Canada. Having beaten them in the 2025 Rugby World Cup final, it is difficult not to see the fixtures as anything other than a three-Test series and Mitchell thinks the prospect is "really cool".

But with England travelling from Manchester to Exeter, to Twickenham, to Canada and the USA, the schedule is a test of its own.

"It's kind of like you're auditioning for Australia 2029 because geographically we're definitely going to be travelling some distance in this tournament," he said.

"So, I think we're trying to mirror that, understand how important our connections are and play exciting rugby."
